```json
{"ranking": ["M4", "R3", "C1"], "fault": "M4 has m=3 instead of m=1. This corrupts the 1:1 active-load mirror (M3/M4) of the op-amp's input pair, so the op-amp no longer gives a clean virtual ground. The bandpass response is then distorted: the peak lands at 26.6 MHz with Q≈2.15, versus about 1.13 expected from the passives."}
```

This is a best guess; I did not simulate. Two things don't add up:

- **The passives don't give a 28 Hz filter either.** With the values as written (pF-range caps), the multiple-feedback bandpass network computes to f0 ≈ 45 MHz. If the caps were really µF, it would be ≈ 45 Hz. Either way it would sit outside the 25.2–30.8 Hz window. No single changed element can move f0 by the ~10⁶ seen in the measurement. That suggests a unit or scaling quirk in the canonical netlist, which I can't resolve from what's given.
- **Why M4 ranks first.** It is the only element that looks structurally wrong: a 3:1 ratio in an active-load mirror is unusual. It would also explain the measured Q (2.15) and centre gain (+2.7 dB) both being higher than the passives predict (Q≈1.13, about −0.4 dB).

R3 and C1 are fallbacks in case the fault is a wrong passive value that shifts f0.
